title: Bram and the Kitchen
premise: Sebastian Whitlock, once a celebrated wedding planner who fled the industry after a scandal that destroyed his career and nearly his life, now runs a modest café kitchen on a remote island, hiding under a new name. When the island's community center assigns anonymous pen-pals to combat winter isolation, he's paired with Marguerite 'Greta' Voss—the prosecutor who once ruined him, herself exiled after refusing to bury evidence against a powerful family. Through letters neither knows the other's identity, they fall into an intimacy neither can afford, until the truth surfaces mid-season and forces both to choose between the safety of their constructed selves and a justice that no court ever delivered. The story ends as the last ferry of the season arrives: Greta stays, Sebastian signs his real name to the café door for the first time, and they plan no wedding at all—only a life.
about_author: Elodie Nystrom is a former hospitality professional who spent a decade planning weddings before trading ballrooms for a writing desk overlooking cold northern water. She writes about people rebuilding themselves in small towns where everyone pretends not to notice.

chapters.title: The Anonymous Correspondence Act
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The community center's pen-pal program launches; Sebastian, coerced by the woman who saved his life with a café job, grudgingly writes his first letter to 'M.' We learn his old name died in a courtroom ten years ago. Emotional beat: guarded reluctance masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Letters to a Stranger
chapters.summary: Greta's POV, in the city she no longer belongs to. She answers the assignment cynically, then finds herself confessing things she's never said aloud—that she prosecuted a case she was pressured to lose, and lost everything when she didn't. Emotional beat: the dangerous relief of anonymity.

chapters.title: Small Safe Steps
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Letters arrive weekly; he begins planning his days around them. A wedding party books the café, forcing him to confront the industry he abandoned. He lies to M. about who he was. Emotional beat: hope arriving like contraband.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Signed the Indictment
chapters.summary: Greta's POV. She recognizes details in her pen-pal's letters—the island, the café, a turn of phrase from the trial transcript. She realizes she's writing to Sebastian Whitlock and says nothing, unable to stop. Emotional beat: guilt entangled with longing.

chapters.title: Off-Season
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Greta Voss arrives on the island as the new interim magistrate; Sebastian recognizes her instantly and nearly flees. They circle each other at the café counter, both hiding that they already know each other by heart. Emotional beat: terror wearing a polite face.

chapters.title: What the Court Never Heard
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Greta reveals in a letter that the Whitlock scandal was manufactured by the Halloran family to bury evidence she'd found; Sebastian realizes his pen-pal knows his case intimately. They meet deliberately as strangers, each testing the other. Emotional beat: two people lying with the truth.

chapters.title: The Mirror Test
chapters.summary: Greta's POV. Sebastian discovers her identity through a dropped letter, and the betrayal detonates: she knew for months. He banishes her from the café. Alone, she admits she protected herself, not him, by staying silent. Emotional beat: the collapse of the safe distance.

chapters.title: Halloran's Men
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The Hallorans, learning Greta is on the island, send threats—her evidence still could reopen the case. Sebastian must decide whether to stay invisible or stand beside the woman who ruined and redeemed him. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into choice.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POV. On the dock, with the Halloran lawyer watching and the ferry boarding, Greta publicly files to reopen the case and Sebastian stands beside her under his real name. Whatever happens, they will not be invisible again. Emotional beat: the price of survival, finally paid together.

chapters.title: A Life, Not a Wedding
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, epilogue in spring. The case moves forward; the café's door is repainted with his true name. Greta stays past the season. They agree never to plan a wedding—only the ordinary, unglamorous work of being seen. Emotional beat: quiet, earned joy.
